item.title: The Diuretic That Tried to Quiet Seizures — Neonatal Electrographic-Only Seizures, Developmental NKCC1/KCC2 Chloride Shift (Rivera/Dzhala), Bumetanide NKCC1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9C0H) & NEMO/Soul Trials
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 84: Neonatal Electrographic-Only Seizures, Developmental NKCC1/KCC2 Chloride Shift (Rivera/Dzhala), Bumetanide NKCC1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9C0H) & NEMO/Soul Trials. item.description: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic feedback in recurrent sulfonylurea hypoglycemia: Gunaratne et al.'s (2018) nocturnal rebound drop from 106 to 25 mg/dL after voriconazole-to-fluconazole CYP2C9 inhibition with gliclazide, Aguilar-Bryan et al.'s (1995) cloning of beta-cell SUR1 gating KATP depolarization, Boyle et al.'s (1993) 8-volunteer crossover comparing dextrose alone, diazoxide, and octreotide, and Fasano et al.'s (2008) double-blind emergency-department octreotide RCT.

item.title: The Rhythm That Changed Its Shape — Flecainide 1:1 Atrial Flutter & Use-Dependent QRS Widening, Cardiac Nav1.5 Pore Block (Jiang 2020) & The CAST Surrogate-Endpoint Paradox
item.description: Ion-channel kinetics and clinical trial epistemology in Class IC antiarrhythmic therapy: Dardas et al.'s (2021/2022) flecainide atrial flutter 1:1 AV conduction with wide-complex tachycardia, Jiang et al.'s (2020 Cell) cryo-EM structure of cardiac Nav1.5 central-cavity flecainide binding, Ranger et al.'s (1989) exercise-amplified use-dependent QRS prolongation from slow unbinding, and the 1989 CAST mortality reversal.

item.title: The Burn That Came Before Relief — TRPV1 Cloning (Caterina 1997), Reversible Epidermal PGP 9.5 Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization & 8% Capsaicin Patch Neuropathic Pain Trials
item.description: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

item.title: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 81: neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia critical-sample diagnostics (simultaneous glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and free fatty acids; Ferrara et al.), repurposing antihypertensive benzothiadiazine diazoxide (Drash & Wolff 1964), beta-cell SUR1/Kir6.2 KATP opening and NN414 comparator structure (PDB 7W4O), dominant KCNJ11 p.Phe55Leu gating vs. recessive focal 11p15 loss, and echocardiographic surveillance for diazoxide-associated pulmonary hypertension (Herrera et al., 7/295).

item.title: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. (2009, 2010) Phase 3 timed 25-foot walk responder denominators (78/224 vs. 6/72; 51/119 vs. 11/118), extended-release vs. oral solution Cmax, and why renal impairment (CrCl <= 50 mL/min) precipitates acute seizures.

item.title: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

item.title: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
item.description: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

item.title: One Ångström Through the Splenic Gate — Red Cell Interendothelial Slits, PIEZO1 Hereditary Xerocytosis (8YEZ/8YFG), Gardos KCNN4 & Ektacytometry
item.description: Squeezing a human erythrocyte through a sub-micron splenic interendothelial slit: PIEZO1 mechanosensitive dome flattening and MDFIC-bound slowed inactivation (PDB 8YEZ/8YFG, 6.1 ms vs. 17.4 ms), Ca2+-activated Gardos (KCNN4) potassium/water efflux, osmotic gradient ektacytometry shifts, and why splenectomy triggers portal/thrombotic catastrophe in PIEZO1 hereditary xerocytosis.

item.title: One Ångström Riding the Flagellum — Sperm Capacitation, CatSper Pore Architecture (7EEB), Whole-Cell Patch Clamp & Hyperactivated Beat
item.description: Atomic and electrophysiological journey along the principal piece of a sperm flagellum: mouse CatSperosome cryo-EM architecture (PDB 7EEB) vs. human cytoplasmic-droplet whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (Lishko/Strunker 2011; Mansell 2014), the 2016 ABHD2 hypothesis vs. 2026 selective inhibitor tests, and CATSPER-deficient IVF failure rescued by ICSI.

item.title: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
item.description: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

item.title: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials
item.description: Biophysics, structural biology, and clinical safety engineering of dofetilide (Tikosyn): Sanguinetti's IKr/hERG discovery, Wang & MacKinnon's human Kv11.1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 5VA2) and Tyr652/Phe656 drug-trapping cavity, reverse use-dependence at slow sinus rates after cardioversion, renal OCT2/MATE1 transport interactions, and the DIAMOND trials.

item.title: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
item.description: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

item.title: The Rhythm That Waited for the Treadmill — CPVT Exercise Stress ECG (H042), Post-Exertional Bidirectional VT, RYR2 Diastolic Calcium Leak & Paired-Test Repeatability
item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H042) investigation of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT): why resting ECGs and structural echocardiography are normal, how adrenergic surge and early post-exercise recovery unmask beat-to-beat alternating bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (Akiba et al. 2026), RYR2 diastolic Ca2+ leak and NCX1 delayed afterdepolarizations (Steinberg et al. 2023), and exercise-test repeatability limits (Peltenburg et al. 2023).

item.title: Why a Visual Signal Can Arrive Late After Sight Improves — Dawson's 1954 Signal Averaging, Halliday's 1972 Pattern-Reversal VEP in Optic Neuritis & Sokol's Dioptric Blur Artifact
item.description: Clinical neurophysiology of pattern-reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP): Dawson's (1954) time-locked signal averaging, Halliday, McDonald & Mushin's (1972) discovery of persistent monocular cortical latency delay after visual acuity recovery in optic neuritis, and Sokol & Moskowitz's (1981) demonstration of refractive blur latency artifacts.

item.title: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
item.description: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

item.title: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
item.description: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

item.title: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
item.description: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

item.title: How Scientists Followed Carbon Through a Tumor — Warburg's 1927 Artery-Vein Lactate Balance, DeBerardinis's 13C NMR Glioblastoma TCA & Glutaminolysis & Hensley's Intraoperative Lung Tumor Infusions
item.description: From the classical Warburg Effect to human intraoperative stable-isotope tracing: Warburg, Wind & Negelein (1927) aerobic glycolysis across rat tumor vessels, DeBerardinis et al. (2007) 13C NMR isotopomer resolution of simultaneous glycolysis, TCA flux, fatty acid synthesis, and glutamine anaplerosis in glioblastoma cells, and Hensley et al. (2016) intraoperative [U-13C]glucose infusions in human NSCLC patients.

item.title: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
item.description: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: How a Touch Becomes a Current — Chick Muscle Stretch Channels (1984), Piezo1/2 RNAi Screen (2010) & Bilayer Reconstitution
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 3: how Guharay & Sachs (1984), Coste et al. (2010, 2012), Ranade et al. (2014), and Syeda et al. (2016) proved that Piezo1 and Piezo2 are the bona fide pore-forming mechanosensitive ion channels underlying vertebrate gentle touch.

item.title: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.title: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

item.title: The Pocket That Did Not Predict the Trial — Fragile X FMR1 Methylation PCR, Grm5 Rescue, Mavoglurant in Human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9), [11C]ABP688 PET & FXLEARN
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 79: FMR1 CGG repeat-primed and HpaII methylation PCR (Chen et al.), Fmr1 x Grm5 genetic cross (Dölen et al. 2007) and CTEP chronic rescue (Michalon et al. 2012), mavoglurant (AFQ056) bound 8 Å below the membrane surface in human mGlu5 (PDB 4OO9, Asn747/Ser805/Ser809), human [11C]ABP688 PET receptor occupancy, why Jacquemont's (2011) 7-person full-methylation subgroup failed prospective replication in Phase 2b (Berry-Kravis et al. 2016), and the FXLEARN pediatric language trial (log10 contrast -0.10, P=.16).

item.title: The Signal That Tested the Pituitary — Ghrelin & GOAT Discovery, Macimorelin Bound to Human GHSR–Gq (PDB 9V2N), 22-kDa GH Immunoassay & ITT Crossover Agreement
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 78: reverse pharmacology from GHSR1a cloning (Howard et al. 1996) to rat stomach ghrelin isolation (Kojima et al. 1999) and GOAT/MBOAT4 Ser3 octanoylation (Yang 2008; Gutierrez 2008), peptidomimetic macimorelin (JMV1843) bound to human GHSR-Gq at 2.63 Å (PDB 9V2N, Asp99/Arg102/Ser123), 22-kDa IDS-iSYS chemiluminescent GH assay, thorough QTcF crossover (+9.61 ms at 4 h), and 139-pair vs. 140-pair diagnostic agreement against the insulin tolerance test (Garcia et al.).

item.title: The Cocaine Signal That Stayed Behind — Cocaine-Associated Chest Pain, Serial hs-cTnI Trajectory, Human DAT-Cocaine Cryo-EM (PDB 9EO4), Benzoylecgonine/Cocaethylene LC-MS/MS & Lange Vasospasm
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

item.title: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

item.title: The Vitamin the Body Couldn't Clear — PTH-Suppressed Hypercalcemia, Human VDR-Calcitriol Structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann's LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D:24,25(OH)2D Ratio & CYP24A1 Loss
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of vitamin D catabolism and CYP24A1 deficiency: why normal 25(OH)D3 with suppressed PTH and elevated 1,25(OH)2D3 points to failed 24-hydroxylase inactivation rather than overdose, the 1.8 Å human VDR-calcitriol crystal structure (PDB 1DB1), Kaufmann & Jones's (2014) PTAD-derivatized LC-MS/MS 25(OH)D3:24,25(OH)2D3 molar ratio diagnostic (>80), and Schlingmann et al.'s (2011) discovery of idiopathic infantile and adult CYP24A1 hypercalcemia.

item.title: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

item.title: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
item.description: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed in the Scan — [18F]FDG from 1976–1979 Brain Autoradiography (Sokoloff & Reivich) and Cyclotron 109.77-Min Decay to GLUT3/Hexokinase II Trapping (4ZW9/2NZT), Thoracic SUVmax 7.2 & EBUS Granulomas
item.description: From cyclotron target to thoracic staging needle: Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]deoxyglucose method and Reivich/Alavi/Phelps's 1976-1979 human [18F]FDG brain studies, Hamacher nucleophilic synthesis and 109.77-minute half-life batch logistics (21 CFR 212.70), D-glucose-bound GLUT3 (PDB 4ZW9) and human hexokinase II (PDB 2NZT) metabolic trapping, 511-keV coincidence physics and SUVbw math (7.2 g/mL), and why bilateral FDG-avid mediastinal nodes still require EBUS-TBNA tissue confirmation (granulomatous inflammation vs. metastasis).

item.title: The Protein That Met Resistance — Mouse 2×2 Dietary Amino Acid & Progressive Weight-Pulling Factorial (Trautman 2023), Sestrin2–Leucine Pocket & GATOR2 Cryo-EM vs. Longland & Layman Human Trials
item.description: Separating body-composition compartments, individual muscle hypertrophy, and glycemic tolerance when dietary protein meets resistance load: Trautman et al.'s (2023) 2x2 mouse amino-acid/weight-pulling factorial (protecting against fat accretion while leaving high-protein glucose intolerance unchanged, P=0.7442), Sestrin2–leucine and GATOR2 structural mechanics, Drummond's human rapamycin biopsy tracer study, and Longland (2016) vs. Layman (2005) human trials.

item.title: The Iron Test Before the School Bell — Non-Anemic Adolescent Iron Deficiency (TSAT 9.5%, Ferritin 10 µg/L), Human Ferroportin–Hepcidin Cryo-EM (6WBV), Alternate-Day Isotope Absorption & Thai vs. Baltimore School Trials
item.description: Separating storage biomarkers from classroom endpoints in iron deficiency without anemia: assay reference intervals vs. WHO/2026 AAP ferritin thresholds, human ferroportin–hepcidin cryo-EM occlusion and Co2+/Fe2+-coupled binding (PDB 6WBV, Kd 210 -> 2.5 nM), Stoffel's erythrocyte stable-isotope absorption trial (16.3% daily vs. 21.8% alternate-day), and Sungthong's Thai school trial (n=397) vs. Bruner's Baltimore verbal-learning RCT (n=81).

item.title: Three Sodium Levels, Two Diets, One Blood Pressure — Controlled DASH-Sodium Feeding Trial (n=412, −8.9 mmHg Path), 24-Hour Urinary Excretion, Human NCC–Hydrochlorothiazide Cryo-EM (9BWT), Urinary Vesicles & GWAS Limits
item.description: Controlled feeding trials meet distal-tubule atomic physiology: Sacks et al.'s (2001) DASH-Sodium parallel-diet/crossover-salt design (n=412, why non-additive interaction yields -8.9 mmHg rather than -12.6 mmHg), energy-scaled sodium density vs. 24h urine potentiometry, human phosphorylated NCC and hydrochlorothiazide cryo-EM (PDB 9BWT), KCl urinary extracellular vesicle readouts, and UK Biobank/CHARGE MTHFS gene-diet slope limits.

item.title: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials
item.description: Atomic pathogenesis and covalent enzyme inhibition in celiac disease: tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) Cys277 thioester deamidation of gliadin glutamine into negatively charged glutamate, HLA-DQ2.5 positively charged P4/P6/P7 pocket anchoring via Lysβ71 (PDB 1S9V), tTG-IgA vs. total IgA and Marsh/villus-height-to-crypt-depth morphometry, and Schuppan et al.'s (2021) NEJM ZED1227 trial.

item.title: The Fat That Never Got Digested — Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency, Fecal Elastase CELA3A/3B ELISA vs. 72-Hour Fat Balance, Lipase-Colipase Lid Opening (1LPB) & Enteric Pancrelipase Trials
item.description: From watery-stool dilution artifacts in fecal elastase testing and Tóth's discovery that 'elastase-1' monoclonals actually measure CELA3B/CELA3A to 72-hour coefficient of fat absorption (CFA) balance math, Egloff's human pancreatic lipase-colipase open-lid crystal structure (PDB 1LPB), enteric-coated pancrelipase pH release kinetics, Whitcomb's 54-patient randomized trial, and fibrosing colonopathy incidence.

item.title: The Fructose That Locked Up Phosphate — Hereditary Fructose Intolerance, KHK Fructose-1-Phosphate Trapping vs. ALDOB A149P/A174D Crystal Structures, 31P-MRS Hepatic PME & KHK Inhibition
item.description: From infant post-weaning hypoglycemia, hypophosphatemia, hyperuricemia, and proximal renal Fanconi syndrome in Hereditary Fructose Intolerance to KHK-driven fructose-1-phosphate sequestration, human ALDOB A149P/A174D crystal structures, hepatic 31P-MRS phosphomonoester dynamics, and investigational ketohexokinase inhibition.

item.title: The Kidney After the Heat — Collecting-Duct AVP–V2R Cryo-EM (7DW9), AQP2 Ser256 Trafficking, Recurrent Rat Fructose Dehydration vs. Human Exercise Heat Crossovers
item.description: Separating physiological water conservation from tubular injury during heat stress and sweetened rehydration: human arginine vasopressin-V2R-Gs cryo-EM structure (PDB 7DW9) and PKA-driven AQP2 apical exocytosis, Chapman et al. (2020) 12-human heat-exercise soft-drink crossover, García-Arroyo et al. (2017) Wistar rat V1a/V2 conivaptan blockade, and Tourula et al. (2026) hypotonic vs. hypertonic sports drinks.

item.title: The Glucose That Couldn't Leave the Liver — Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia, ER G6PC1 His176 Phosphohistidine Catalysis vs. SLC37A4, Uncooked Cornstarch & DTX401 Gene Therapy
item.description: From acute fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in glycogen storage disease type Ia to ER lumenal G6PC1 His176 phosphohistidine hydrolysis vs. SLC37A4 glucose-6-phosphate transport, Grefhorst's ChREBP/LXRalpha mouse blockade vs. human [6,6-2H2]glucose flux, uncooked cornstarch therapy, and AAV8 G6PC1 gene replacement.

item.title: The Sugar That Stayed After the Milk Was Gone — Classic Galactosemia, GALT Ping-Pong His186 Catalysis (5IN3), Endogenous [1-13C]Galactose Production & Aldose Reductase
item.description: Why lifelong dietary galactose restriction saves neonates from acute hepatorenal crisis yet fails to prevent long-term speech and ovarian complications in classic galactosemia: human GALT double-displacement His186 uridylylation (PDB 5IN3), Berry et al. [1-13C]galactose isotope-dilution proof of ~1 g/day endogenous galactose synthesis, and aldose reductase galactitol reduction.

item.title: The Hormone That Heard Less Protein — Dietary Protein Restriction, Hepatocyte FGF21 Induction, Beta-Klotho 5VAQ Docking, FAP Cleavage & Intact vs. Total ELISA
item.description: Endocrine and structural dissection of human FGF21 induction during low-protein and sucrose feeding (Nicolaisen, Ramne, Laeger): C-terminal beta-Klotho docking (PDB 5VAQ), fibroblast activation protein (FAP) Pro171 cleavage separating intact bioactive FGF21 from total immunoreactive FGF21, and central Klb macronutrient preference circuits.

item.title: The Leucine That Wouldn’t Clear — Maple Syrup Urine Disease, BCKDH E1 Phosphorylation (1DTW/1OLS), Isobaric LC-MS/MS Alloisoleucine & Liver Transplant Flux
item.description: Biochemical and analytical dissection of Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) decompensation: human BCKDH E1 alpha-ketoacid decarboxylation and BCKDK Ser292 phosphorylation (PDB 1DTW/1OLS/4H7Q), chromatographic separation of isobaric leucine, isoleucine, alloisoleucine, and hydroxyproline at m/z 132->86, LAT1 blood-brain barrier competition, IV BCAA-free rescue, and liver transplantation.

item.title: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
item.description: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

item.title: What the Colon Sends Back — Inulin Fermentation, Eudragit Colon-Targeted [1-13C]SCFAs, Systemic Availability (36% Acetate, 9% Propionate, 2% Butyrate) & FFAR2 8J24
item.description: Atomic and clinical tracing of colonic short-chain fatty acids (Boets et al. 2015, 2017; Bloemen et al. 2009): Bacteroides ovatus inulin cleavage, Roseburia/Faecalibacterium acetate-to-butyrate cross-feeding, Eudragit S100 colon-targeted [1-13C]SCFA capsules with IV [2H]SCFA clearance calibration (36% acetate, 9.2% propionate, 2.4% butyrate systemic availability), and human FFAR2 cryo-EM (PDB 8J24).

item.title: Three Roads to Liver Fat — Chylomicron NEFA Spillover, Multi-Tracer Liver Biopsies, Human FASN 9MJ9 & Beverage De Novo Lipogenesis
item.description: Quantitative isotope dissection of hepatic triacylglycerol sources across three human studies: Piché et al. (2018) chylomicron-derived [U-13C]palmitate spillover, Donnelly et al. (2005) 4-day triple-tracer liver biopsies (59% NEFA, 26% DNL, 15% dietary within accounted fraction), human FASN cryo-EM (PDB 9MJ9), and Geidl-Flueck et al. (2021) sugar-sweetened beverage VLDL-palmitate secretion.

item.title: The Carbon in the Next Breath — [U-13C6]Fructose Meal Oxidation, KHK-A 2HW1 Active Site, GC-C-IRMS Plasma Glucose & 7T Hepatic Deuterium Imaging
item.description: Stable-isotope tracing of ingested [U-13C6]fructose in humans (Theytaz et al. 2014): GLUT5 uptake, ketohexokinase KHK-A vs. KHK-C phosphorylation (PDB 2HW1), aldolase B cleavage, GC-C-IRMS 13C-glucose and breath 13CO2 recovery, paired with 7-Tesla hepatic deuterium metabolic imaging (Brunasso et al. 2026).

item.title: One Ångström Under the Mucus — Human Airway Axonemal Dynein (PDB 8J07), Periciliary Brush Exclusion, DNAH5 Splice Defects & Nasal Nitric Oxide
item.description: Atomic-to-clinical journey through mucociliary clearance and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD): human airway doublet microtubule structure (Walton et al. 2023, PDB 8J07), periciliary brush osmotic exclusion (Button et al. 2012), nasal nitric oxide chemiluminescence, and DNAH5 intronic splice-site RT-PCR.

item.title: One Ångström When the Artery Opens — Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion, Succinate Accumulation, Complex I Reverse Electron Transport & Infarct Salvage
item.description: Atomic and clinical timeline of the first minutes after coronary artery reperfusion: Jennings & Reimer's (1960/1977) canine wavefront of necrosis, coronary-sinus succinate release, Complex I flavin site reverse electron transport (RET) superoxide burst upon reoxygenation, and why ischemic postconditioning failed to reduce clinical STEMI endpoints.

item.title: One Ångström Across the Gut Barrier — Enteric Translocation, TLR4–MD-2 Lipid A Dimerization (3FXI), Microvascular Shunting & Septic Shock
item.description: From an injured intestinal barrier and mesenteric lymph node cultures (Deitch 1989) to the crystal structure of human TLR4-MD-2 bound to E. coli Ra LPS (PDB 3FXI), sublingual microvascular shunting (De Backer 2002), endothelial glycocalyx shedding, and why eritoran MD-2 blockade failed in the Phase III ACCESS sepsis trial.

item.title: One Ångström from a Dividing Cell — Paclitaxel in the β-Tubulin Taxane Pocket (1JFF), Cremophor Anaphylaxis & Mitotic Spindle Fate
item.description: Atomic-scale journey into the luminal beta-tubulin taxane pocket (PDB 1JFF): distinguishing Cremophor EL complement-mediated infusion anaphylaxis from delayed neutropenia, M-loop lateral protofilament stabilization, and multipolar mitotic spindle catastrophe in human tumors.

item.title: How the End of a Pathway Slows the Beginning — Yates & Pardee's Pyrimidine Feedback, Gerhart & Schachman's Dissociated Catalytic vs. Regulatory ATCase Subunits & the 1965 MWC Allosteric Model
item.description: Birth of molecular allostery: from Yates & Pardee's (1956) pyrimidine end-product inhibition in E. coli to Gerhart & Pardee's (1962) heat-desensitized aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase), Gerhart & Schachman's (1965) separation and reassembly of catalytic and regulatory subunits, and the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (1965) conformational equilibrium model.

item.title: How Scientists Saw ATP Synthase Turn — Abrahams & Walker's Asymmetric F1 Crystal States, Noji & Yoshida's Spinning Actin Filament (120° Steps) & Itoh's Magnetic-Bead Mechanical ATP Synthesis
item.description: Direct proof of rotary catalysis in F1-ATPase: Abrahams et al. (1994) 2.8 Å crystal snapshot of three distinct catalytic β conformations around an asymmetric γ axle, Noji et al. (1997) single-molecule fluorescence microscopy of unidirectional counterclockwise γ rotation and Yasuda et al. (1998) discrete 120° steps, and Itoh et al. (2004) electromagnet-driven clockwise rotation forcing net ATP synthesis.

item.title: How a Cell Pumps Ions Uphill — Skou's 1957 Crab-Nerve Na++K+-Synergistic ATPase, Post's Phosphoenzyme Intermediate, Garrahan & Glynn's 3 Na+:2 K+:1 ATP Stoichiometry & Goldin's Inside-Out Vesicles
item.description: Enzymology and vectorial reconstitution of the sodium-potassium pump: Skou (1957) discovery of the Mg2+/Na+/K+-activated ATPase in Carcinus maenas nerve membranes, Post, Sen & Rosenthal (1965) acyl-phosphate intermediate formed with Na+ and hydrolyzed with K+, Garrahan & Glynn (1967) 3 Na+ : 2 K+ : 1 ATP coupling ratio in resealed red-cell ghosts, and Goldin (1977) inside-out liposome reconstitution.

item.title: How a Cell Senses Low Oxygen — Semenza's EPO 3' Enhancer & HIF-1α/β Purification, Maxwell's VHL Ubiquitin-Tagged Normoxic Degradation & Ivan/Jaakkola's Pro564 Oxygen-Dependent Hydroxylation
item.description: Molecular mechanism of cellular oxygen sensing: Semenza et al. (1991) & Wang et al. (1995) identification of the hypoxia-response element and HIF-1α/ARNT heterodimer, Maxwell et al. (1999) proof that pVHL targets HIF-α for oxygen-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal destruction, and Ivan et al. (2001) & Jaakkola et al. (2001) discovery of enzymatic Pro564 4-hydroxylation as the direct oxygen switch.

item.title: How a Potassium Channel Chooses an Ion — Bezanilla & Armstrong's Squid Axon Na+ Block, Heginbotham's TVGYG Signature Mutations & Doyle & MacKinnon's KcsA Selectivity Filter
item.description: Atomic solution to the potassium channel selectivity paradox: Bezanilla & Armstrong (1972) >10:1 K+/Na+ selectivity and internal Na+ block in perfused squid axons, Heginbotham et al. (1994) TVGYG pore-loop mutagenesis converting a K+-selective pore into a nonselective cation channel, Doyle et al. (1998) & Zhou et al. (2001) 2.0 Å KcsA crystal structures showing backbone carbonyl cages matching dehydrated K+, and Thompson et al. (2009) planar Na+ binding.

item.title: How a Cell Builds a Droplet in the Right Place — C. elegans P Granules, Brangwynne's Shear-Induced Dripping & FRAP Recovery, MEX-5 Gradient Dissolution & MEG-3 Scaffolding
item.description: Discovery of intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation: Hird et al. (1996) live GFP::PIE-1 imaging of C. elegans P granules, Brangwynne et al. (2009) proof of liquid wetting, fusion, ~second FRAP exchange, and spatial condensation/dissolution asymmetry, and Smith et al. (2016) & Folkmann et al. (2021) MEX-5 RNA competition and intrinsically disordered MEG-3 surface clusters.
