item.title: The Switch That Keeps Us Awake — Hypothalamic Orexin/Hypocretin Discovery, Canine HCRTR2 & Human CSF Orexin-A Deficiency in Narcolepsy Type 1, OX2R Crystal Structures (4S0V/7L1U) & Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists
item.description: From wake-maintenance physiology to targeted insomnia pharmacology: 1998 discovery of hypothalamic hypocretins/orexins, 1999 canine HCRTR2 and murine knockout narcolepsy models, human CSF orexin-A <=110 pg/mL cutoff in ICSD-3 narcolepsy type 1, structural comparison of antagonist-bound (PDB 4S0V) vs. agonist-bound (PDB 7L1U) OX2R, and clinical trials and next-morning safety of suvorexant and daridorexant.

item.title: Lithium and the Level That Came Back — Cade & Schou, Lithium-Heparin Tube Artifacts, GSK-3β Mg2+ Competition, ENaC Nephrogenic DI & Post-Dialysis Rebound
item.description: Clinical and molecular dissection of lithium toxicity: lithium-heparin green-top collection tube false elevations (Wills et al.), GSK-3β and IMPase Mg2+ competition (PDB 1PYX, 2BJI), collecting-duct ENaC entry (PDB 6BQN) and AQP2 downregulation, and EXTRIP hemodialysis rebound kinetics.

item.title: Foxglove, Digoxin & the Number That Rose After Rescue — Withering's Dropsy, Na+/K+-ATPase 4RET, DigiFab Immunoassay Interference & Free vs. Total LC-MS/MS
item.description: From William Withering's 1785 dropsy cases to the 4 A porcine Na+/K+-ATPase crystal structure (4RET), UHPLC-MS/MS MRM transitions, and why ovine DigiFab rescue causes total serum digoxin immunoassays to surge twelvefold while free pharmacologically active digoxin plummets.

item.title: Windows, Workloads, and Diffusing Gas — Ambulatory ECG Cadence & EMBRACE/CRYSTAL AF Trials (H041), Exercise Stress Physiology, HRR & ISCHEMIA (H042) & Plethysmographic Lung Volumes & DLCO/KCO (H043)
item.description: Clinical Cluster & Cardiopulmonary Physiology synthesis of ambulatory ECG monitoring (H041), cardiac exercise stress testing (H042), and lung volumes/DLCO (H043): Barrett's paired patch cohort (n=146), EMBRACE (n=572) & CRYSTAL AF (n=441), nocturnal vagal variants, and toothbrush pseudo-VT; coronary autoregulation, ST localization laws, LBBB vasodilator rule, Cole's HRR (n=2,428), WOMEN & ISCHEMIA; and Boyle's Law plethysmography vs. gas dilution, Roughton-Forster DLCO/KCO physics, CPFE/PAH phenotypes, ppo-DLCO, and race-neutral GLI Z-scores.

item.title: The Drug That Took the Long Way — Parkinson's Vallecular Tablet Retention on Videofluoroscopy, Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC Gut Decarboxylation & Oral vs. Jejunal Levodopa-Carbidopa Gel Kinetics
item.description: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

item.title: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

item.title: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
item.description: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

item.title: The Signal That Outlasted the Cigarette — Exhaled CO vs. Urine Cotinine & Anabasine on Nicotine Patch, Langley's Receptor Concept, Human alpha4-beta2 nAChR Varenicline Cryo-EM (6UR8) & the EAGLES Trial
item.description: From John Newport Langley's 1905 'receptive substance' to transplant tobacco abstinence verification: human alpha4-beta2 nAChR cryo-EM structure bound to varenicline (PDB 6UR8), cytisine-to-varenicline partial agonist design, CYP2A6 nicotine-to-cotinine kinetics, LC-MS/MS separation of isobaric nicotine and minor tobacco alkaloid anabasine (m/z 163), and the 8,144-participant EAGLES trial.

item.title: The Flush That Fooled the Numbers — Extended-Release Niacin vs. Nicotinamide, Goldberger's Pellagra, HCAR2/GPR109A Cryo-EM (8IJA), Langerhans PGD2/DP1 Flushing & AIM-HIGH/HPS2-THRIVE Trial Futility
item.description: From pellagra prevention to the HDL surrogate fallacy: nicotinic acid vs. nicotinamide chemistry, human HCAR2/GPR109A cryo-EM structure bound to niacin (PDB 8IJA), Langerhans-cell and keratinocyte PGD2/DP1 flushing vs. laropiprant blockade, glycine-conjugation vs. amidation metabolic saturation, and the AIM-HIGH and HPS2-THRIVE cardiovascular outcome trials.

item.title: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
item.description: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

item.title: The Inheritance in Thin Air — 5,100-Year-Old Zongri Genomes, Denisovan EPAS1 Introgression, Hypoxia Enhancer ENH5 Editing & Endothelial Adaptation
item.description: Evolutionary genomics and functional regulatory biology of high-altitude adaptation on the Tibetan Plateau: 89 ancient genomes spanning 5,100 years beginning at Zongri (Wang et al. 2023), Denisovan-like EPAS1 haplotype introgression and selection timing (Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014; Zhang et al. 2021), hypoxia-responsive ENH5 enhancer reporter and deletion experiments (Gray et al. 2022), and iPSC-derived endothelial transcriptomics under hypoxia (Gray et al. 2025).

item.title: The Reference Sample Had Changed — Post-Transplant Forensic DNA Chimerism Across Blood (100% Donor), Buccal Swabs (Mixed Leukocyte Infiltration) & Hair/Eyebrow Follicles
item.description: Forensic genetics of biological chimerism after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation: why blood reference samples convert completely to the donor's STR and amelogenin sex profile, why buccal swabs yield variable donor-recipient DNA mixtures due to mucosal leukocyte trafficking, and why hair shafts and eyebrow follicles remain reliable recipient reference tissues (Jacewicz et al. 2013; Li et al. 2014; 2026 eyebrow follicle study).

item.title: The Seed the Scan Could Not Name — Adult Occult Sapodilla Seed Aspiration (Nguyen Phan 2026), Two-Year Unilateral Wheeze & Flexible Bronchoscopy Extraction (H049)
item.description: Pulmonary diagnostics and flexible bronchoscopy (H049) for occult adult airway foreign bodies: Nguyen Phan et al.'s (2026) two-year missed sapodilla seed aspiration masquerading as recurrent right-lower-lobe pneumonia and asthma, radiolucent organic foreign-body CT physics, granulation-tissue tumor mimics, and flexible vs. rigid bronchoscopic retrieval across adult cohorts (Jang et al. 2022; Purohit et al. 2023).

item.title: The Movement After the Missing Breath — Video-Polysomnography (H044), Obstructive Sleep Apnea Arousal Pseudo-RBD vs. True REM Sleep Without Atonia & CPAP Resolution
item.description: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H044) investigation of nocturnal dream-enactment mimics: how synchronized video-polysomnography (EEG, EOG, submental/limb EMG, nasal pressure, and thoracoabdominal effort belts) separates true alpha-synucleinopathy REM sleep behavior disorder (sustained/phasic REM sleep without atonia) from severe obstructive sleep apnea respiratory-arousal pseudo-RBD that resolves completely on CPAP (Deguchi et al. 2021; Bergmann et al. 2024).

item.title: The Breath the Spirometer Missed — Normal Spirometry with 31% Predicted DLCO, Plethysmographic Lung Volumes, Combined Fibrosis & Emphysema (CPFE) & ERS/ATS Standards
item.description: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H043 (Lung Volumes & Diffusing Capacity): why a patient can have FVC 112% predicted and TLC 88% predicted alongside a single-breath DLCO of 31% predicted (Neder et al. 2019), how opposing mechanical effects of emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis preserve lung volumes while destroying alveolar-capillary gas transfer (Kim et al. 2022 IPF-PRO registry, N=934; Barisione et al. 2014), and the 2017 ERS/ATS single-breath CO uptake standard (Graham et al. 2017).

item.title: The Seconds That Grew After the Fall — Stetson & Eagleman's 31-Meter Free-Fall Flicker Experiment, Oddball Predictability & Duration vs. Passage-of-Time Judgments
item.description: Experimental psychophysics of subjective time dilation and duration judgment: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman's (2007) 31-meter, 2.49-second free-fall experiment separating retrospective stopwatch expansion (2.96 s recalled vs. 2.17 s imagined, +36%) from unchanged wrist-LED flicker resolution, Pariyadath & Eagleman's (2007) visual oddball duration vs. pitch/flicker dissociation, and Martinelli & Droit-Volet's (2022, N=803) separation of numerical duration estimates from passage-of-time feelings.

item.title: How a Vitamin Can Change a Blood Test’s Result — Green's 1963 Avidin-Biotin Kinetics, Streptavidin Capture Immunoassays, Trambas Spiking/Depletion Controls & Sandwich vs. Competitive Interference
item.description: Biochemical kinetics and clinical laboratory physics of biotin immunoassay interference: Green's (1963) radiotracer measurement of avidin-biotin association/exchange, Bayer & Wilchek's (1974) affinity-capture chemistry, Trambas et al.'s (2018) paired serum biotin-spiking and streptavidin-depletion reversal experiments, and Li et al.'s (2017) human supplementation crossover demonstrating opposite interference directions in sandwich vs. competitive immunoassays.

item.title: How a Flash Test Separates the Retina’s Responses — Adrian's 1945 Red/Blue Scotopic-Photopic ERG, Dilated-Pupil Control, Miyake's Electronegative CSNB Waveform & ISCEV Standards
item.description: Retinal electrophysiology and clinical waveform dissection: Edgar Adrian's (1945) human corneal-thread ERG separating scotopic and photopic responses across wavelengths with dilated-pupil controls, Miyake et al.'s (1986, N=64) electronegative bright-flash ERG in congenital stationary night blindness (preserved photoreceptor a-wave with reduced ON-bipolar b-wave), and 2022 ISCEV full-field and On-Off ERG standards.

item.title: How Pancreas Tests Separate Secretion from Sample Dilution — Burton's 1960 Secretin-Pancreozymin Challenge, Endoscopic Bicarbonate Crossover, Stool Elastase & Lyophilized Water Correction
item.description: Gastrointestinal physiology and specimen physics of exocrine pancreatic testing: from Bayliss & Starling's (1902) secretin discovery and Burton et al.'s (1960) duodenal secretin-pancreozymin aspiration to endoscopic vs. tube bicarbonate crossover validation (Stevens et al. 2006), fecal elastase immunoassay validation (Löser et al. 1996), and Fischer et al.'s (2001) paired freeze-drying experiment showing 16/151 diarrheal stool samples normalize once corrected for water dilution.

item.title: How B12 Testing Separates Supply from Absorption — Castle's 1929 Intrinsic Factor Experiment, Schilling's 1953 Two-Stage Radiotracer Assay, Methylmalonic Acid & Anti-IF Antibodies
item.description: Hematologic and biochemical physiology of vitamin B12 diagnostics: Castle's (1929) sequential extrinsic-plus-intrinsic factor reticulocyte experiments, Schilling's (1953) two-stage radiolabeled urinary absorption test with and without intrinsic factor replacement, and modern three-axis serum cobalamin, methylmalonic acid (MMA), and intrinsic-factor antibody testing.

item.title: How a Blood Test Keeps a History of Glucose — Rahbar's 1968 Diabetic Hemoglobin Fraction, Bunn's 1976 59Fe-Transferrin Glycation Kinetics, Red-Cell Age & the ADAG Trial
item.description: Biochemistry and hematologic kinetics of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c): Rahbar's (1968) discovery in diabetic erythrocytes, Bunn et al.'s (1976) 59Fe-transferrin pulse-chase proof of slow non-enzymatic postsynthetic Amadori glycation, Fitzgibbons et al.'s (1976) density-fraction proof of erythrocyte age dependence, and Nathan et al.'s (2008) ADAG calibration.

item.title: What an Ear Test Learns by Changing the Pressure — Terkildsen & Thomsen's 1959 Pressure Sweep, Jerger's 1970 Type A/B/C Curves, Equivalent Canal Volume & Infant 1,000 Hz Probes
item.description: Acoustic immittance physics and developmental biomechanics of tympanometry: Terkildsen & Thomsen's (1959) ear-canal pressure-sweep compliance peak, Jerger's (1970) Type A/B/C diagnostic classification, Mehta et al.'s (2006) equivalent ear-canal volume (Vec) three-way disambiguation of flat Type B traces, and Gellrich et al.'s (2024) myringotomy-validated proof of 1,000 Hz vs. 226 Hz probe tones in young infants.

item.title: How an Eye Scan Finds Layers with Light — Fercher's 1988 Low-Coherence Eye-Length Interferometry, Huang & Fujimoto's 1991 Retinal OCT & Preperimetric Glaucoma RNFL Loss
item.description: Optical physics and clinical translation of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): why femtosecond light propagation requires interferometric path-length matching rather than direct electronic clock timing, Fercher et al.'s (1988) low-coherence axial eye-length interferometry, Huang, Swanson & Fujimoto's (1991) cross-sectional retinal OCT invention, and Miki et al.'s (2014) longitudinal proof of structural RNFL thinning preceding visual field defects in glaucoma.

item.title: Why a Pulse Oximeter Needs a Pulse — Millikan & Wood's Bloodless Ear Zero, Takuo Aoyagi's 1974 Pulsatile AC/DC Ratio, Dyshemoglobin 85% Artifacts & Skin-Pigment Bias
item.description: Optical physics and physiological limitations of pulse oximetry: Millikan (1942) and Wood & Geraci's (1949) pneumatic bloodless-ear zeroing, Takuo Aoyagi's (1974) breakthrough using pulsatile arterial AC/DC absorbance ratios at two wavelengths, two-wavelength degrees-of-freedom failure in carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia, and melanin/low-saturation occult hypoxemia bias (Bickler et al. 2005; Sjoding et al. 2020).

item.title: How a Test Maps Vision Away from Where You're Looking — Goldmann's 1945 Hemispherical Kinetic Bowl, Heijl & Krakau's 1975 Automated Blind-Spot Fixation & 20/20 Chiasmal Hemianopia
item.description: Psychophysics and neuro-ophthalmic anatomy of visual field perimetry: Goldmann's (1945) standardized luminance hemispherical bowl and kinetic target-velocity reaction-time artifact, Heijl & Krakau's (1975) automated computerized static threshold perimetry and blind-spot catch trials, and Ogra et al.'s (2014) proof that optic chiasm compression routinely produces bitemporal visual field loss despite 6/6 (20/20) foveal acuity.

item.title: How an Electrode Learned to Measure Glucose — Clark & Lyons's 1962 Enzyme Membrane Electrode, Updike & Hicks's 1967 Dual-Cathode Differential Sensor & Basu's 2013 Interstitial Lag
item.description: Electrochemical and physiological foundations of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM): Clark & Lyons's (1962) enzyme-membrane electrode concept, Updike & Hicks's (1967) dual-cathode active-vs-inactivated polyacrylamide 'enzyme electrode' canceling ambient oxygen drift, subcutaneous interstitial fluid sensing and electroactive drug interference, and Basu et al.'s (2013) human tracer microdialysis proof of physiological capillary-to-interstitial glucose lag.

item.title: What a Bright Spot on a PET Scan Is Made Of — Sokoloff's 1977 [14C]Deoxyglucose Hexokinase Trap, Reivich & Phelps's 1979 Human [18F]FDG-PET & Kubota's 1992 Macrophage Microautoradiography
item.description: Biochemical basis and diagnostic specificity of [18F]FDG-PET (H022): Sokoloff et al.'s (1977) hexokinase metabolic trapping of 2-deoxyglucose-6-phosphate, Reivich & Phelps's (1979) human positron emission tomography translation, Som et al.'s (1980) oncologic uptake, and Kubota et al.'s (1992) cellular microautoradiography proving why activated macrophages and granulation tissue generate intense FDG avidity indistinguishable from cancer on a single SUV number.

item.title: How a Sleep Study Tells Why Breathing Stopped — Gastaut's 1965 Simultaneous EEG/Airflow/Effort Recording, Sullivan's 1981 Nasal CPAP Pneumatic Splint & PSG vs. Home Testing Denominators
item.description: Historical physiology of polysomnography and sleep-disordered breathing (H044): Gastaut, Tassinari & Duron's (1965–1966) polygraphic separation of obstructive, central, and mixed apneas by comparing airflow against thoracoabdominal effort, Sullivan et al.'s (1981) nasal CPAP pneumatic splint experiment, and the denominator divergence between EEG-verified total sleep time in polysomnography and recording/monitoring time in home sleep apnea testing (Bianchi & Goparaju 2017).

item.title: Why a Pinhole Can Sharpen a Blurry Letter — Snellen's 5-Arcminute Optotypes, Bailey-Lovie LogMAR Charts, Campbell & Gregory's 2 mm Aperture & Eagan's Retinal-Illumination Trap
item.description: Physiological optics of clinical visual acuity and refraction (H051): Snellen's (1862) 5-arcminute optotype standard, Bailey & Lovie's (1976) proportional logMAR chart design, Campbell & Gregory's (1960) tradeoff between geometrical blur circles and diffraction across pupil diameters, Eagan et al.'s (1999) demonstration of pinhole retinal-dimming pseudoworsening in maculopathy, and Donders (1864) / Sankaridurg et al. (2017) on cycloplegic vs. non-cycloplegic refraction.

item.title: How a Brain Recording Can Reveal a Response Without Movement — Owen's 2006 Tennis/Navigation fMRI Imagery, Sitt's 2014 EEG Complexity Markers & Claassen (2019) / Bodien (2024) Cognitive Motor Dissociation
item.description: Detecting covert command-following in behaviorally unresponsive brain-injured patients: Owen et al.'s (2006) fMRI mental-imagery paradigm, Sitt et al.'s (2014) quantitative EEG markers in disorders of consciousness, Claassen et al.'s (2019) bedside motor-command EEG classifier identifying cognitive motor dissociation and predicting 1-year functional recovery, and Bodien et al.'s (2024) six-center cohort quantifying both prevalence (25%) and negative-result sensitivity limits.

item.title: How a Newborn Hearing Screen Listens for an Answer — Jewett & Williston's 1971 Averaged ABR Waves, David Kemp's 1978 Outer-Hair-Cell Otoacoustic Emissions & Starr's 1996 Auditory Neuropathy Paradox
item.description: Objective physiological hearing screening without behavioral responses: Jewett & Williston's (1971) time-locked signal averaging of microvolt auditory brainstem responses (ABR), David Kemp's (1978) discovery of active cochlear outer-hair-cell otoacoustic emissions (OAE), NICU screening validation (Stevens et al. 1990), and Starr et al.'s (1996) discovery of auditory neuropathy with preserved OAEs and absent ABR.

item.title: How a Sealed Booth Measures the Air Left in Your Lungs — Hutchinson's 1846 Vital Capacity Spirometer, DuBois's 1956 Boyle's-Law Body Plethysmograph & Trapped Emphysematous Gas vs. Helium Dilution
item.description: From Hutchinson's 1846 spirometer to DuBois's 1956 body plethysmograph (H043): why standard spirometry cannot measure residual volume, applying Boyle's pressure-volume law across a closed airway shutter inside a sealed cabin, and why plethysmography captures non-communicating bullae and trapped emphysematous gas missed by single-breath helium dilution (Bedell et al. 1956; O'Donnell et al. 2010).

item.title: How a Treadmill ECG Tests the Heart Under Load — Master's 1929 Two-Step Test, Bellet's 1961 Radio-Telemetry Exercise Recording, Bruce's 1963 Multistage Treadmill Protocol & the Duke Treadmill Score
item.description: From two-step challenges to multistage exercise stress testing (H042): Master & Oppenheimer's (1929) standardized step workload, Bellet et al.'s (1961) radiotelemetry during exercise vs. recovery, Bruce et al.'s (1963) graded multistage treadmill protocol, and Mark et al.'s (1987, 1991) Duke treadmill score integrating exercise time, ST deviation, and symptoms.

item.title: How an Eye-Pressure Test Reads Through the Cornea — Schiøtz Indentation, Goldmann & Schmidt's 1957 3.06-mm Applanation Tear-Film & Corneal Stiffness Balance, Ehlers's Cannulated Eye Study & OHTS Corneal Thickness
item.description: Biomechanics of intraocular pressure measurement through the cornea (H052): Schiøtz (1905) indentation vs. Goldmann & Schmidt's (1957) small-area 3.06-mm applanation balancing tear-film capillarity against corneal stiffness, Ehlers et al.'s (1975) direct intracameral manometry demonstrating corneal thickness bias, and OHTS (2002) risk stratification.

item.title: How One Breath Tests Gas Transfer — Marie Krogh's 1915 Paired Breath Samples, Ogilvie & Forster's 1957 Helium-Dilution Single-Breath DLCO & Roughton-Forster Membrane vs. Red-Cell Partitioning
item.description: From Marie Krogh's 1915 diffusion experiments to modern single-breath DLCO (H043): paired breath-hold sampling, Ogilvie & Forster's (1957) inert helium tracer dilution separating airspace mixing from true vascular uptake, Roughton & Forster's (1957) serial membrane and erythrocyte resistance model, and clinical interpretation of DLCO, VA, and KCO.

item.title: How the ECG Learned to Follow You Home — Waller's 1887 Limb Recordings, Einthoven's Calibrated Quartz String Galvanometer, Holter's 1961 Portable Tape Recorder & Barrett's 2014 24-Hour vs. 14-Day Patch Comparison
item.description: From bedside galvanometers to ambulatory rhythm monitoring (H041): Waller's (1887) limb-contact control ruling out mechanical chest movement, Einthoven's (1903) calibrated string galvanometer, Holter's (1961) portable battery-powered recorder, and Barrett et al.'s (2014) paired 146-patient comparison showing why the adhesive patch's diagnostic advantage over 24-hour Holter monitoring (96 vs. 61) came from extended sampling duration rather than Day-1 superiority (52 vs. 61).

item.title: How an Audiogram Finds Which Ear Heard the Tone — Fletcher & Wegel's 1922 Calibrated Thresholds, Transcranial Bone-Conduction Crossover, Denes & Naunton's Narrowband Noise & Hood's 1957 Masking Plateau
item.description: Acoustics and clinical logic of pure-tone audiometry and contralateral masking (H050): Fletcher & Wegel's (1922) calibrated receiver thresholds, skull-vibration crossover to the non-test cochlea, Denes & Naunton's (1952) frequency-band masking efficiency, and J.D. Hood's (1957) plateau method separating cross-heard responses from true ear-specific air- and bone-conduction thresholds.

item.title: How a Blood Test Tracks the Insulin Your Body Makes — Berson & Yalow's 1956–1960 Competitive 131I-Insulin Radioimmunoassay, Melani's 1970 Serum C-Peptide Separation & Modern Two-Antibody Electrochemiluminescence
item.description: How an unexpected antibody artifact became the foundation of clinical endocrinology: Berson & Yalow's (1956-1960) competitive radioimmunoassay (where rising unlabeled hormone lowers the bound-to-free tracer ratio), Melani, Rubenstein & Steiner's (1970) detection of equimolar co-secreted C-peptide in human serum, and modern two-antibody electrochemiluminescent C-peptide testing in insulin-treated patients.

item.title: How a Sea Slug Gets Used to a Touch — Pinsker's Aplysia Gill-Withdrawal Habituation, Castellucci & Kandel's 1974 Quantal Failure Analysis & Bailey & Chen's Electron-Microscopy Presynaptic Active Zones
item.description: From behavioral habituation to synaptic quantal release and ultrastructure in Aplysia: Pinsker et al.'s (1970) gill-withdrawal habituation and dishabituation, Castellucci & Kandel's (1974) quantal variance/failure proof that short-term habituation reflects fewer transmitter packets released per impulse rather than smaller postsynaptic unit responses, and Bailey & Chen's (1983) electron microscopy of long-term habituated sensory-neuron varicosities.

item.title: When the Same Taste Signal Leads to Opposite Choices — Chandrashekar's Dish Bitter Receptor Screen, Zhao & Mueller's RASSL Spiradoline Routing & Human TAS2R16 Expressed in Mouse Sweet vs. Bitter Cells
item.description: Labeled-line coding in mammalian taste: separating molecular ligand detection in heterologous cells (Chandrashekar et al. 2000; Bufe et al. 2002 TAS2R16) from behavioral attraction vs. aversion in mice when the exact same engineered receptor (spiradoline RASSL, Zhao 2003) or human bitter receptor (TAS2R16, Mueller 2005) is expressed in T1R2 sweet cells vs. T2R bitter cells.

item.title: How a Blood Vessel Tells Itself to Relax — Furchgott & Zawadzki's 1980 Intact vs. Rubbed Rabbit Aorta, Rubanyi's Donor-Detector Perfusion, Palmer & Moncada's Ozone Chemiluminescence Nitric Oxide Proof & 15N-Arginine Tracing
item.description: How the vascular endothelium's relaxing signal was identified as nitric oxide: Furchgott & Zawadzki's (1980) discovery that removing the inner endothelial lining abolishes acetylcholine relaxation while preserving smooth-muscle contraction, Rubanyi et al.'s (1985) upstream donor/downstream denuded detector bioassay, Palmer, Ferrige & Moncada's (1987) chemiluminescent nitric oxide measurement alongside Ignarro's cGMP comparison, and 15N-arginine precursor tracing.

item.title: How a Cell Detects an Energy Shortfall — Carling & Hardie's Shared ACC/HMG-CoA Reductase Kinase (AMPK), Hawley's Thr172 & LKB1–STRAD–MO25 Complex, Sanders's PP2Cα Protection & Gowans's AMP vs. ADP Allostery
item.description: Dissecting the eukaryotic energy sensor AMPK: Carling, Zammit & Hardie's (1987) discovery that a single AMP-responsive kinase inhibits both fatty-acid and sterol synthesis, Hawley et al.'s identification of Thr172 phosphorylation by LKB1–STRAD–MO25, Sanders et al.'s (2007) cell-free proof that AMP binding shields Thr172 from dephosphorylation, and Gowans et al.'s (2013) separation of ADP/AMP protection from AMP allosteric catalysis.

item.title: How a Cell Opens Its Own Calcium Store — Streb, Irvine, Berridge & Schulz's 1983 Permeabilized Acinar IP3 Release, Ferris's Purified IP3 Receptor Lipid Vesicles & Callamaras's Confocal Puffs-to-Waves
item.description: How second-messenger calcium mobilization from internal stores was proven step by step: Streb, Irvine, Berridge & Schulz (1983) IP3-triggered Ca2+ release in permeabilized pancreatic acinar cells, Ferris et al. (1989) reconstitution of purified IP3 receptor into artificial lipid vesicles proving one protein both binds IP3 and forms the Ca2+ channel, and Callamaras et al. (1998) optical flash-photolysis puffs and waves.

item.title: How a Locust Turns Sound into Current — Michelsen's Abdominal Frequency Tuning, Windmill's Laser-Scanned Tympanum Waves, Warren's Auditory Receptor Currents & Chaiyasitdhi's 2-µm Axial Pull vs. Push
item.description: Biophysics of insect tympanal hearing in the desert locust: Michelsen's (1968) receptor frequency tuning, Windmill et al.'s (2008) laser-vibrometry frequency-sorting waves across the abdominal tympanum, Warren & Matheson's (2018) isolated transduction currents, and Chaiyasitdhi et al.'s (2025 reviewed preprint) direct 2-µm cap pull vs. push recordings.

item.title: How Scientists Found a Cycle in Cell Respiration — Krebs & Johnson's 1937 Pigeon-Breast Oxygen Flasks (342 to 1,385 µL), Malonate Succinate Trapping Under O2 vs. N2 & Stern-Ochoa Condensing Enzyme
item.description: How Krebs & Johnson (1937) proved cell respiration runs in a catalytic cycle rather than a linear chain: super-additive oxygen uptake with trace citrate in minced pigeon breast muscle, malonate blockade trapping succinate forward from citrate and oxaloacetate under oxygen, citrate resynthesis from oxaloacetate, and Stern, Ochoa & Lynen's (1951-1952) purified citrate synthase step.

item.title: How a Cell Builds Insulin from One Chain — Sanger's Two-Chain Disulfide Puzzle, Steiner & Oyer's 1967 Human Islet Tumor Pulse-Chase Proinsulin Precursor & Equimolar C-Peptide Secretion
item.description: Discovery of prohormone processing: why isolated insulin A and B chains recombine inefficiently in vitro, Steiner & Oyer (1967) identification of single-chain proinsulin in human islet-cell adenoma slices, pulse-chase proof of intracellular proteolytic conversion into two-chain insulin, and Rubenstein, Clark & Steiner (1969) equimolar C-peptide co-secretion enabling clinical distinction between endogenous and exogenous insulin.

item.title: How Cells Tie Growth to Available Nutrients — Heitman & Hall's Yeast FPR1/TOR1/TOR2 Rapamycin Mutants, Sabatini & Brown's Mammalian mTOR Affinity Capture & Hara's Amino-Acid Withdrawal Gate
item.description: Discovery of the TOR nutrient-sensing pathway: Heitman, Movva & Hall (1991) genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae showing rapamycin requires FKBP12 (FPR1) to inhibit TOR1/TOR2, Sabatini et al. (1994) & Brown et al. (1994) biochemical capture of the ~289 kDa mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) only when rapamycin is bound to FKBP12, Barbet et al. (1996) starvation-like translation arrest, and Hara et al. (1998) amino-acid gating of insulin-stimulated p70S6K phosphorylation.

item.title: How a Sour Taste Starts — Huang's PKD2L1 Sour-Cell Ablation, Chang's Apical Proton Current, Tu's Otop1 Proton Channel Cloning & Teng/Zhang's Chorda Tympani Nerve Loss in Otop1-/- Mice
item.description: From cell-type ablation to the molecular proton sensor for sour taste: Huang et al. (2006) selective elimination of PKD2L1 taste cells erasing chorda tympani acid responses while sparing sweet, salty, bitter, and umami, Chang, Waters & Liman (2010) direct measurement of apical proton entry, Tu et al. (2018) discovery of the OTOP1 proton channel, and Teng et al. / Zhang et al. (2019) in vivo Otop1-/- requirement for sour nerve signaling.

item.title: When the Lips Change the Sound You Hear — Sumby & Pollack's Speech-in-Noise Gain, McGurk & MacDonald's Ba/Ga→Da Fusion & Beauchamp's Superior Temporal Sulcus TMS Disruption
item.description: Multisensory speech integration and causal cortical testing: Sumby & Pollack (1954) audiovisual enhancement in noise across vocabulary set sizes, McGurk & MacDonald (1976) cross-modal syllable fusion where auditory /ba/ paired with lip-articulated /ga/ yields heard /da/, and Beauchamp, Nath & Pasalar (2010) fMRI-guided TMS over the superior temporal sulcus selectively reducing McGurk fusion while sparing congruent control syllables.

item.title: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase
item.description: Discovery of the second-messenger principle: Rall, Sutherland & Berthet (1957) two-stage cell-free assay separating particulate membrane hormone response from soluble phosphorylase activation via a dialyzable, heat-stable factor, Sutherland & Rall (1958) chemical identification of cyclic 3',5'-AMP, and Walsh, Perkins & Krebs (1968) discovery of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).

item.title: Why an Aroma Can Seem to Come from Your Mouth — Rozin's Dual-Olfaction Juice Test, Dalton's Subthreshold Saccharin-Benzaldehyde Integration, Small's Retronasal fMRI & Blankenship's Optogenetics
item.description: Neurobiology of retronasal olfaction and flavor referral: Rozin (1982) dual-sense hypothesis, Dalton et al. (2000) subthreshold benzaldehyde + saccharin integration (28% lower threshold vs. null MSG control), Small et al. (2005) nasal-cannula fMRI showing route-dependent brain activation for identical vapor concentrations, and Blankenship et al. (2019) gustatory cortex requirement for rapid retronasal learning.

item.title: How a Burst Leaves a Synapse Stronger — Bliss & Lømo's 1973 Perforant-Path LTP Controls, Collingridge's APV NMDA Blockade & Tsien's CA1-Restricted NR1 Knockout
item.description: Experimental dissection of hippocampal Long-Term Potentiation (LTP): Bliss & Lømo (1973) pathway-specific potentiation lasting hours in rabbit dentate gyrus, Collingridge, Kehl & McLennan (1983) selective NMDA antagonist APV blocking LTP induction while sparing baseline AMPA synaptic transmission, and Tsien, Huerta & Tonegawa (1996) postnatal CA1 NR1 knockout mice.

item.title: How a Robin Reads the Tilt of a Magnetic Field — Wiltschko's 1972 Horizontal vs. Vertical Coil Flips, Ritz's Radio-Frequency Disruption & Xu's European Robin Cryptochrome 4
item.description: Biophysics of the avian inclination compass: Wiltschko & Wiltschko (1972) proof that European robins read magnetic field line dip angle (poleward vs. equatorward) rather than polarity, Ritz et al. (2004) diagnostic radio-frequency spin resonance disruption, and Xu et al. (2021) transient absorption spectroscopy of purified migratory European robin vs. non-migratory chicken/pigeon Cryptochrome 4.

item.title: How Scientists Recorded a Single Ion Channel — Katz & Miledi's Acetylcholine Noise Variance, Neher & Sakmann's 1976 Frog Muscle Pipette Steps & Hamill's Gigaseal Configurations
item.description: From statistical fluctuation analysis to direct single-molecule electrophysiology: Katz & Miledi (1972) inferring elementary acetylcholine events from voltage noise, Neher & Sakmann (1976) resolving discrete ~2.2 pA square current steps across a micro-patch of denervated frog muscle, and Hamill et al. (1981) gigaohm glass-membrane seals enabling cell-attached, whole-cell, inside-out, and outside-out configurations.

item.title: When the Same Sound Becomes a Surprise — Sutton's P300 Uncertainty Cue, Bekinschtein's Local-vs.-Global Oddball Hierarchy & Wacongne's Omitted-Tone Prediction Error
item.description: Electrophysiology of auditory expectation and hierarchical prediction error: Sutton et al. (1965) P300 discovery comparing identical clicks under certainty vs. uncertainty, Bekinschtein et al. (2009) local-global paradigm where a locally Deviant XXXXX/XXXXY sequence becomes the global rule, and Wacongne et al. (2011) brain responses to an omitted expected tone.

item.title: How Light Sets the Body Clock — Rodless/Coneless Circadian Phase Shifts, Berson's Retrograde SCN Ganglion Cells, Melanopsin Knockout Rescue & Opn4Diphtheria Ablation
item.description: Discovery of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs): Freedman et al. (1999) intact circadian photoentrainment without rods and cones, Berson, Dunn & Takao (2002) intrinsic light responses in SCN-projecting ganglion cells after synaptic isolation, Hattar et al. (2003) triple-knockout loss of entrainment when rods, cones, and melanopsin are removed together, and Güler et al. (2008) ipRGC cell ablation.

item.title: How Infants Tune In to Speech — Werker & Tees's 6-to-12-Month Head-Turn Narrowing, Maye's Bimodal vs. Unimodal Distributions, Kuhl's Live-vs.-Video Mandarin & Lytle's Peer Contingency
item.description: Perceptual narrowing in infant speech acquisition: Werker & Tees (1984) preservation of English contrasts alongside loss of non-native Hindi/Salish discrimination by 10–12 months, Maye, Werker & Gerken (2002) statistical bimodal vs. unimodal distribution reshaping, Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003) live vs. televised Mandarin tutors, and Lytle, Garcia-Sierra & Kuhl (2018) peer-paired contingent video.

item.title: What an Eye Movement Can Tell Us About Dreaming — Aserinsky & Kleitman's 1953 EOG Awakenings, Dement's Duration Judgments, Foulkes's Definition Shift & Siclari's Posterior Hot Zone
item.description: From Aserinsky & Kleitman's (1953) discovery of Rapid Eye Movement sleep and Dement & Kleitman's (1957) 5-vs.-15-minute binary duration judgments to Foulkes's (1962) proof that NREM mental activity depends on definition thresholds and Siclari et al.'s (2017) posterior cortical low-frequency reduction predicting dream experience within both REM and NREM sleep.

item.title: The Mirror-Image Test for an Opioid Receptor — Goldstein's Stereospecificity, Pert & Snyder's [3H]Naloxone Levorphanol vs. Dextrorphan Assay & Enkephalin Discovery
item.description: Biochemical proof of brain opioid receptors: Goldstein et al. (1971) enantiomeric competition concept, Pert & Snyder (1973) [3H]naloxone vacuum-filtration assay showing stereospecific displacement by (-)-levorphanol but not (+)-dextrorphan, Hughes et al. (1975) discovery of endogenous pentapeptides Met- and Leu-enkephalin, and 1992 delta-receptor cloning.

item.title: How the Nose Builds an Odor Code — Buck & Axel's Olfactory Receptor Family, Zhao's Adenoviral I7 Pairing, Malnic's Combinatorial Code & Bozza's Bulb Glomeruli
item.description: Molecular logic of combinatorial olfaction: Buck & Axel (1991) cloning of the odorant receptor superfamily, Zhao et al. (1998) functional pairing of receptor I7 with octanal, Malnic et al. (1999) single-neuron calcium imaging + RT-PCR showing concentration-dependent recruitment (2 to 5 to 8 receptors for bromooctanoic acid), and Bozza et al. (2004) in vivo glomerular synapto-pHluorin maps.

item.title: How the Ear Turns Up Its Own Volume — Brownell's Outer Hair Cell Electromotility, Zheng's Prestin Discovery & Dallos's Stiffness-Preserving Knock-In
item.description: Biophysics of the cochlear amplifier: Brownell et al. (1985) voltage-driven length changes in guinea-pig outer hair cells, Zheng et al. (2000) subtractive cloning of prestin (SLC26A5), Liberman et al. (2002) 40–60 dB threshold shift in prestin-/- mice, and Dallos et al. (2008) 499-prestin knock-in separating active motor force from passive axial stiffness.

item.title: Why a Chili Pepper Feels Hot — Caterina & Julius's TRPV1 Expression-Cloning Screen, Thermal Activation, Knockout Hyperalgesia & Chicken-Rat Chimeras
item.description: Discovery and dissection of polymodal nociception via TRPV1: Caterina et al. (1997) Fura-2 expression cloning from dorsal root ganglia, physical heat (>43°C) gating of the capsaicin receptor, Caterina et al. (2000) TRPV1-/- loss of inflammatory thermal hyperalgesia, and Jordt & Julius (2002) separation of capsaicin and thermal gating in avian-mammalian chimeras.

item.title: A Chemical Signal Comes in Packets — Fatt & Katz Miniature Endplate Potentials, Del Castillo & Katz Poisson Quantal Failures & Heuser-Reese Quick-Freeze Exocytosis
item.description: Statistical and ultrastructural proof of quantal synaptic transmission: Fatt & Katz (1952) spontaneous miniature endplate potentials, del Castillo & Katz (1954) independent quantal content estimates (0.57 by amplitude ratio vs. 0.56 by Poisson failure fraction), and Heuser & Reese (1979) 3–5 ms quick-freeze electron microscopy.

item.title: How a Shark Finds a Fish Under Sand — Murray's Ampullae of Lorenzini Recordings, Kalmijn's Agar-Chamber & Dipole Strikes & Sawfish Electrosense
item.description: Experimental proof of passive electroreception in elasmobranchs: Murray (1962) ampullae of Lorenzini nerve recordings, Kalmijn (1971) catshark and skate strikes at agar-screened live plaice vs. polyethylene insulation vs. artificial bioelectric dipoles, and Wueringer et al. (2012) sawfish rostral electrosense.

item.title: When GABA Pulls Voltage the Other Way — KCC2 Chloride Extrusion, Gramicidin-Perforated Patch Anion Reversal & Microglial BDNF in Neuropathic Pain
item.description: Ionic basis of GABAergic polarity switches: Rivera et al. (1999) KCC2 antisense knockdown in hippocampal neurons, Coull et al. (2003, 2005) gramicidin-perforated patch recordings in spinal lamina I after nerve injury (-72.6 mV to -49.0 mV) driven by microglial BDNF-TrkB signaling, and depolarizing shunting conductance.

item.title: The Butterfly That Steers by a Clock — Monarch Phase-Shifted Flight Simulators, Antennal Circadian Clocks & Conflicting Black-vs.-Clear Enamel Inputs
item.description: Neuroethology of the monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: Mouritsen & Frost (2002) ±6h photoperiod shifts (225° vs. 136° vs. 335°), Merlin et al. (2009) antennal light-entrained circadian oscillators, and Guerra et al. (2012) rescue of group orientation by amputating a desynchronized black-painted antenna.

item.title: When One Eye Takes the Lead — Wiesel & Hubel's Monocular vs. Binocular Deprivation, Critical Period Timing & Pizzorusso's Perineuronal Net Chondroitinase
item.description: Synaptic competition and critical period closure in visual cortex: Wiesel & Hubel (1963–1970) why monocular suture shifts cortical drive (1/84 cells) while binocular suture preserves responsiveness, and Pizzorusso et al. (2002) extracellular matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan digestion in adult rats.

item.title: A Message That Traveled in Blood — Bayliss & Starling's 1902 Denervated Jejunal Loop, the Discovery of Secretin, Peptide Sequencing & Receptor Cloning
item.description: Birth of endocrinology and humoral signaling: Bayliss & Starling (1902) surgically denervated jejunal loop acid challenge, intravenous jejunal vs. ileal extract controls Separating pancreatic secretion from vasodepression, Mutt et al. (1970) porcine secretin purification, and Ishihara et al. (1991) secretin receptor cAMP signaling.

item.title: How Chloroplasts Made ATP in the Dark — Mitchell's Chemiosmotic Hypothesis, Jagendorf & Uribe's Acid-Bath pH Jump & Racker-Stoeckenius Chimeric Vesicles
item.description: Decisive experimental tests of chemiosmotic coupling: Mitchell (1961), Jagendorf & Uribe (1966) spinach thylakoid acid-bath pH jump (141 vs. 12 nmol ATP/mg chlorophyll in darkness), and Racker & Stoeckenius (1974) halobacterial bacteriorhodopsin + bovine mitochondrial ATP synthase proteoliposomes.

item.title: How a Bat Measures the Dark — Pierce & Griffin's Ultrasonic Detector, Galambos's Obstacle Course & Simmons's Electronic Echo-Delay Target Illusion
item.description: Experimental discovery of bat echolocation: Pierce & Griffin (1938) ultrasonic heterodyne detector, Griffin & Galambos (1941) reversible sight vs. hearing vs. vocalization blocks, terminal buzz pursuit (1960), and Kick & Simmons (1984) electronic delay-line phantom targets.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: Can an Active Neuron Use Glucose Directly? — Astrocyte-Neuron Lactate Shuttle (1994) vs. Peredox NADH Imaging (2017)
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 4: testing the Astrocyte-Neuron Lactate Shuttle (Pellerin & Magistretti 1994) with single-neuron Peredox NADH/NAD+ fluorescence lifetime imaging and MCT1/2 blockade in hippocampal slices and awake mice (Diaz-Garcia et al. 2017).

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: What Does a Nerve Impulse Cost? — Squid Giant Axon Voltage Clamp (1952) vs. Mammalian Mossy-Fiber Na+ Load (2009)
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 2: separating net voltage change from opposing Na+ and K+ fluxes—from Hodgkin & Huxley's (1952) squid axon model to Alle, Roth & Geiger's (2009) action-potential clamp in rat hippocampal mossy fibers showing 1.3x capacitive minimum Na+ entry.

item.title: How We Learned to Read a Cell: A Flash in the Dark — Hecht-Shlaer-Pirenne Thresholds (1942), Baylor Single-Rod Suction Pipettes (1979) & cGMP Gating
item.description: On the Shoulders of Giants Historical Teaching Pilot 1: from Hecht, Shlaer & Pirenne's (1942) 5-14 photon human psychophysical threshold to Baylor, Lamb & Yau's (1979) 1 pA single-photon suction-pipette recordings in toad rod outer segments and Fesenko et al.'s (1985) inside-out patch cGMP gating proof.
